title: MCP Apps
description: The official extension for interactive UI elements, such as charts and forms, rendered inline in a conversation.
question: Can a server contribute interactive UI through this framework?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: Apps is the part of MCP that produces something a user manipulates rather than reads. An agent framework without a surface to render it into can only answer with absence; cataloguing it records that rather than leaving it unasked.

notes.openai-agents: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: does not declare `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`, so a server cannot offer it UI.
notes.pydantic-ai: Pydantic AI 2.54.0: does not declare `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`, so a server cannot offer it UI.
notes.mastra: Mastra 2.2.0: declares `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` on every session, unconditionally. This row measures that declaration only, not whether an app resource is rendered as anything an agent or user can use.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): createMCPClient declares no `extensions` by default, so the fixture's `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` offer goes unanswered. The package exports `mcpAppClientCapabilities` for a caller to pass as `capabilities` to declare MCP Apps support; that opt-in was not measured.
notes.strands: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `MCPClient` declares no extensions, `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` included, so a server cannot offer it UI.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the client declares no extensions, so it never negotiates MCP Apps; the SDK has no option to declare one.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: the fastmcp `Client` `MCPTools` builds declares no extensions, so the `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` extension the fixture offers is never used.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: neither DSPy nor the caller's `mcp.Client` declares extensions, so `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` is never negotiated.
notes.langchain_js: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): the client declares no `extensions`, and no `MCPAdapter` option passes one through, so the fixture's `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` offer goes unanswered.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): the client declares no `extensions`, and no session option passes one through. The fixture offered `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `DefaultMcpClient` declares no extensions, so the fixture's `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` extension is never negotiated.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): the client declares no `extensions`. mcptoolset has no extension option, and the only route is `ClientCapabilities.Extensions` in the go-sdk `ClientOptions` of the caller's `*mcp.Client`.
notes.ms_agent_framework_dotnet: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): the client declares no `extensions`, and `McpClientOptions` passed through no option for one. The fixture offered `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`.
